ashwin (eng-runtime): quick RFC follow-up — i sketched a tighter contract between the allocator and memory tiers (host/gpu/ssd). want to sync on compatibility and rollout plan. TL;DR: make "resident token" explicit, keep a soft-hint path for migration :wave

maria (eng-runtime): can you paste the proposed API surface here? curious how it affects per-tenant accounting and eviction signals

ashwin (eng-runtime): sure. two small primitives: a hard reserve (returns token) and a soft hint. idea: hard reserve guarantees pages stay resident until token drop; soft hint only biases eviction. prototyping signature:```
// hard reserve
ReserveResident(tenant_id string, bytes int, tier string) -> token string, err
ReleaseResident(token string) -> err

// soft hint
HintResident(tenant_id string, bytes int, tier string, priority int) -> ok bool
```

kevin (eng-ml): hard reserve seems strong — how do we prevent tenants from DOSing GPU memory? quota + token TTL? also need fallback behaviour for dedicated vs hosted

maria (eng-runtime): +1 on quota + TTL. also need an escape hatch: allocator should be able to preempt low-priority tokens under pressure (revocable tokens). that keeps semantics but lets us recover 

ashwin (eng-runtime): exactly. thinking: tokens have lease semantics and a revocation callback. flow: ReserveResident -> runtime returns token + lease_end; on contention, runtime asks owner to Release or runtime force-revoke with callback. revocations are logged and exposed as metric.

kevin (eng-ml): question about fragmentation: if many small tokens live, GPU free space becomes fragmented and hurt large-allocation tails. any compaction plan?

ashwin (eng-runtime): good point. we discussed a compaction API earlier, but this RFC ties into it. options:
- run periodic compaction that migrates free holes (costly)
- encourage callers to request aligned/resizable allocations
- expose a "coalesce_hint(token_list)" where caller indicates tokens that can be reshuffled together

maria (eng-runtime): coalesce_hint sounds promising for model loading flows (we can pause small allocations and re-request contiguous blocks during cold start). fallback to checkpoint+rebuild for worst case.

eva (eng-infra): infra concerns: private deployments may not accept force-revoke behaviour without customer approval. need config flags: `allow_force_revoke` and `revocation_policy` per deployment. also rollout: safe default for existing clusters must be all-soft-hints until opt-in.

ashwin (eng-runtime): noted. propose migration plan:
1) land soft-hint path (no token changes) — low risk
2) add telemetry + quota meters (tenant_resident_bytes, resident_token_count, forced_revokes)
3) enable hard-reserve behind feature flag + per-deployment opt-in
4) add compaction/coalesce APIs next quarter

kevin (eng-ml): what telemetry exactly? we should have both alloc-side and runtime-side:
- tenant_resident_bytes
- resident_request_rate (hard/soft)
- resident_grant_latency_ms
- eviction_ops_by_tier
- forced_revokes_total

maria (eng-runtime): also track fragmentation heuristics: largest_contiguous_free_bytes, fragmentation_ratio = 1 - (largest_free / total_free) per-gpu

ashwin (eng-runtime): yes. I'll add metric names to the RFC.

maria (eng-runtime): for API ergonomics: provide an async path: ReserveResidentAsync(...) that returns a future token so callers can do background warmup without blocking critical path. and a small helper in SDK: `with_resident(ctx, bytes, tier) { /* callback holds token */ }`

kevin (eng-ml): SDK helpers will make adoption easier. also recommend a stress test: run our mem-fuzzer with mixed small/large workloads and measure tail latency + OOMs. local command: `./tools/mem-fuzz --gpus 4 --workload mix-small-large --duration 30m`

deploy-bot: canary deployment for branch `memory-tier-contracts` succeeded on cluster `staging-a` (build 2026.03.21-789) :white_check_mark:

ashwin (eng-runtime): nice. next steps/actions:
- ashwin: update RFC with token TTL/lease and revocation callback (ETA EOD tomorrow)
- maria: add SDK helper pseudo-API & migration guide (ETA 2d)
- kevin: add mem-fuzz scenario + baseline metrics (ETA 3d)
- eva: add deployment knobs for private clusters and opt-in checklist (ETA 2d)

maria (eng-runtime): can someone own the compaction API design? would like to bundle with the allocator refactor.

kevin (eng-ml): i can pair on compaction designs with ashwin — have some sketch for hole-chasing vs async migration that maps to model load patterns

ashwin (eng-runtime): perfect. will update RFC and ping channel when ready. please drop quick replies if any gating concerns. :thumbsup:
